question.text: About 40 members of the Parliament in the UK represent this country, home to the cities of Gwynedd and Swansea.
question.clue: The border between this country and its eastern neighbor is roughly outlined by Offa's dike, which is named after the Mercian king who had it built.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous plots in history.
swap.text: King James I was targeted during this plot, in which a group of Catholics led by Robert Catesby attempted to blow up a section of Parliament. Guy Fawkes Night, often celebrated in the UK with bonfires, marks the anniversary of this plot's failure.
swap.answerHtml: the Gunpowder Plot [or the Gunpowder Treason Plot or the Jesuit Treason]
swap.clue: A letter of warning sent to Lord Monteagle thwarted this event, which was planned by Roger Catesby.

question.leadin: This ruler's most significant victory was preceded by a landing at Pevensey.
question.text: Name this Norman who was crowned on Christmas 1066 after winning the Battle of Hastings over Harold Godwinson.
question.answerHtml: William I (accept William the Conqueror; accept William the Bastard)
question.clue: An Archbishop of Canterbury named Stigand stands next to this ruler in one depiction commissioned by his half-brother Odo.

swap.text: Metal from cannons captured at Sevastopol has been said to be used to make these British awards for "most conspicuous bravery." This award was introduced by its namesake monarch during the Crimean War.
swap.clue: This medal, a cross pattee made from gunmetal, was awarded to 7 members of the defenders at Rorke's Drift, and 18 of them were awarded for actions performed during the Second Relief of Lucknow. It is the highest military decoration in the United Kingdom.

question.leadin: She was also known as Alexandrina.
question.text: Name this monarch whose reign was the longest in British history until Elizabeth II's overtook it in 2015.
question.clue: After the death of her husband, Prince Albert, this ruler only ever wore black.

swap.text: The Williamite War began after this 1688 event that resulted in the passage of the English Bill of Rights. A letter from the "Immortal Seven" sparked this event in which William and Mary took the English throne.
swap.clue: This event was sparked after Mary of Modena gave birth to a son, and an attempt to reverse it failed at the Battle of the Boyne.

question.text: This king, the successor to Edward the Confessor, won the Battle of Stamford Bridge before losing to William the Conqueror at Hastings.
question.answerHtml: Harold Godwinson [or Harold II; or Harold Godwineson; prompt partial answers]
question.clue: The Bayeux Tapestry depicts this monarch being shot in the eye with an arrow.

swap.text: This rebel began the fight for Scottish independence. He won at Stirling Bridge with Andrew Moray but was defeated the following year at Falkirk.
swap.clue: This man was sworn in as the defender of his nation in the Auld Kirk in Selkirk, capital of the Ettrick forest.

question.leadin: John Milton refuted a book attributed to this author point-by-point in Eikonoklastes.
question.text: Name this author who allegedly wrote the pious diary Eikon Basilike. This ruler's death was preceded by Pride's Purge, in which some members of Parliament were blocked from entering the House of Commons.
question.answerHtml: Charles I [or Charles Stuart; prompt on Charles; prompt on Stuart]
question.clue: This ruler was depicted "at the hunt" by his court painter, Anthony van Dyck.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about European rulers with mental disabilities.
swap.text: This king was insane for the last eight years of his life, during which Spencer Perceval was assassinated and the British helped win the Napoleonic Wars.
swap.clue: During this ruler's reign, John Wilkes led troops against men who had destroyed Newgate Prison to protest the Papists Act.

question.text: This man was the actual prime minister during the end of the Seven Years War, having formed an uneasy partnership with Pitt. A longtime Secretary of State, he served a previous stint as prime minister at the beginning of the war, only to be forced out when Britain started off slowly.

swap.leadin: The Norman English adopted this weapon after it was used against them by the Welsh in the 11th century.
swap.text: What weapon was able to fire arrows up to 100 yards with accuracy?
swap.clue: This weapon, most commonly made of yew, does not recurve and reaches from the ground to the height of its user.

question.leadin: This law stated that the requirement to own land was to merely live in a house with a hearth sufficient to boil a pot.
question.text: Identify this 1832 law that massively changed the English and Welsh electoral system, expanded the franchise and eliminated so-called "pocket" and "rotten boroughs".
question.answerHtml: Representation of the People Act 1832 [Accept Great Reform Act 1832 or 1832 Reform Act or First Reform Act]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about appearances of the adjective "black" in British history.
swap.text: A royal regiment from this region was known as the "Black Watch." This mountainous region of Scotland was home to many clans.
swap.clue: The late appearance of one group in this region to take a loyalty oath led to the Glencoe massacre.

question.leadin: Everyday life in early modern England could be dangerous. For instance, in 1558 Thomas Alsopp was killed when one of these objects fell onto the wall he was leaning against, knocking a stone onto his head.
question.text: Name these objects, associated with Catholicism and banned in 1644 as a 'Heathenish vanity'. The present church of St-Mary-le-Strand stands on the site of one made to celebrate the Restoration.

swap.leadin: It was also known as the pitchfork rebellion after the unusual weapons wielded by some at the battle of Sedgemoor.
swap.text: Name this 1685 rebellion whose participants were harshly punished with the Bloody Assizes.
swap.clue: A landing at Lyme Regis began this event, which also involved a coronation at Taunton.

question.leadin: The Titanic was the pride and joy of the White Star Line. Name some things about that company.
question.text: At the time of the Titanic sinking, this businessman was the leader of the White Star Line. He was vilified in the press for surviving the disaster.
question.clue: This chairman of White Star Line was widely vilified in the Hearst Press for not dying on the Titanic and instead leaving in one of the limited number of lifeboats. He is played by Jonathan Hyde in the film Titanic.

swap.leadin: This man talked about the youth of his nation in the "Hug a Hoodie" Speech.
swap.text: Identify this leader who appointed Nat Wei to be the "tsar" of his domestic program, the Big Society.
swap.clue: In August 2011, this leader controversially proposed that social media might be restricted during riots, such as the ones which swept his capital earlier that month.

question.text: After returning from signing the Munich Agreement, Neville Chamberlain gave an infamous speech at the Heston Aerodrome in which he made this four-word proclamation.
question.answerHtml: “peace for our time” [accept “peace in our time”]
question.clue: After acceding to the Munich Agreement, Chamberlain was widely quoted claiming he had achieved this four word phenomenon. Ironically, Hitler began occupying the Sudetenland the next day.

swap.text: Enabled by the Suppression Act of 1536, Cromwell oversaw this policy of Henry's reign which consisted of closing down various Catholic institutions and confiscating their wealth.
swap.clue: This protracted event in the reign of Henry VIII that saw the blighting and closing of several Catholic religious institutions.
